To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current creative industry/ economy discourse has been instrumental in the marginalization and devaluation of cultural policies and their capacity for social and political transformation.

The 'culture economy' discourse has been a major factor in the marginalization of the arts and culture, and the social character of cultural production, in the last 30 years; The creative industry/ economy rhetoric has been used by policy makers at all levels, and by advocates for the arts, to justify the cooption of culture for the purposes of economic development, and to promote the idea that culture can and should generate economic value; The creative industries agenda is a product of a particular political imaginary

(a) The creative industries agenda is a problematic policy trend, (b) The creative industries discourse has been adopted by policy makers and practitioners, (c) The creative industries have been coopted into mainstream public policy, (d) The creative industries rhetoric has generated an obfuscating discourse, (e) The creative industries are a problematic policy trend.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the way that the creative industries discourse has been adopted and applied to the cultural policy field, and the way that the rhetoric of 'culture economy' is used to justify and legitimise cultural policy in ways that are often at odds with the original intentions of cultural policy, and which have a negative impact on the arts and cultural sector, and the communities and individuals it serves.
the ways in which the 'creative' has been co-opted by the 'economy' and how the social character of cultural production is being lost.
the ways in which culture is being redefined as an economic resource in the service of global capitalism, with the consequence that the social and political functions of culture are being undermined
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 'creative industries' agenda has been a disaster for the arts and for culture, and that the creative industries agenda has been a triumph for those in the business of culture, but not for those who are the business of culture.
the current dominant policy discourse is a failure and that it has failed in its own terms.
the creative industries and creative cities agenda has not been a success for the arts and cultural policy community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the creative industries agenda is a crisis in cultural policy.

the 'creative industries' discourse has been used to promote a particular form of neoliberal economic development, and that this has been achieved at the expense of a broader, more socially inclusive and more democratic vision for the future of culture in society.
the current policy trends are not only inadequate to the challenges of the present, but also that they are actively damaging.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the creative industries agenda is not only an inadequate policy framework, but is also a dangerous one, and the article concludes with a call for an alternative approach to culture and economy, and for an alternative political imaginary. (C) 2014 The Authors.
the creative industries discourse has not only failed to deliver on its promise of economic growth but has actually been detrimental for the arts and cultural sector.
the creative industries discourse has been a major factor in the erosion of the cultural policy field, and that the current crisis of cultural policy is the consequence of this erosion.
